lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Judges tells of Israel after Joshua's death, repeatedly falling into idolatry, being oppressed, crying out and being delivered by judges, and ends with the refrain that there was no king in Israel and everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the cycle of sin, oppression, crying out and deliverance in Judges?
ev: Describe the repeating pattern in Judges 2:11-19
Name several judges and the enemies they faced
Say what 21:25 says about Israel at the end

nodes.t: Judah's victories and tribes that failed to drive out the Canaanites
nodes.d: After Joshua's death Judah and Simeon fight first, Othniel wins Achsah, and the chapter lists tribes that did not drive out the inhabitants; the angel of the LORD at Bochim says this disobedience will leave the nations as snares.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened after Joshua died and why the angel spoke at Bochim?
ev: Say who went up first against the Canaanites (1:1-2)
Name some tribes that did not drive out the inhabitants (1:27-33)
Say what the angel of the LORD said and how the people responded (2:1-5)

nodes.d: After Joshua's generation a new generation forgets the LORD and serves Baal; he gives them to enemies, raises up judges to deliver them, and leaves nations to test Israel, who also intermarry and serve their gods.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the pattern that repeats through the book of Judges?
ev: Retell the pattern in 2:11-19
Say why the LORD left nations in the land (2:20-22, 3:1-4)

nodes.d: Israel serves the king of Mesopotamia for eight years; when they cry out the LORD raises up Othniel, on whom the Spirit comes, and the land has rest forty years.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Othniel became Israel's first judge?
ev: Retell the first oppression and deliverance in Judges
Say what is said about the Spirit of the LORD and Othniel (3:10)

nodes.d: Israel serves Eglon of Moab eighteen years; the left-handed Ehud kills Eglon with a hidden dagger, leads Israel to defeat Moab, and the land has rest eighty years; Shamgar also delivers Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of Ehud and how Moab was subdued?
ev: Retell how Ehud killed Eglon
Say what Ehud did after escaping (3:27-30)
Say what Shamgar did (3:31)

nodes.d: Under Jabin's oppression Deborah the prophetess calls Barak to fight Sisera; the LORD routs Sisera's chariots and Jael kills Sisera in her tent.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how God gave victory over Sisera through Deborah, Barak and Jael?
ev: Retell why Deborah summoned Barak (4:6-7)
Say how the LORD gave victory (4:14-16)
Say what Jael did (4:17-22)

nodes.t: The song of Deborah and Barak
nodes.d: Deborah and Barak sing praise to the LORD for the victory, honour the tribes that came and rebuke those that stayed away, bless Jael, and picture Sisera's mother waiting in vain.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the song of Deborah celebrates?
ev: Say who sings the song and whom it praises (5:1-3)
Name tribes praised or blamed (5:14-18, 5:23)
Say how long the land had rest (5:31)

nodes.d: Midian oppresses Israel seven years and Israel cries out; the angel of the LORD calls Gideon, who tears down his father's altar of Baal by night, and then asks for a fleece sign.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how God called Gideon and what signs he asked for?
ev: Retell how the angel of the LORD found Gideon
Say what Gideon did to the altar of Baal (6:25-32)
Describe the fleece sign (6:36-40)

nodes.d: The LORD reduces Gideon's army to three hundred; after hearing a Midianite dream, Gideon surrounds the camp with trumpets, pitchers and lamps and the LORD sets the Midianites against each other.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Gideon defeated Midian with three hundred men?
ev: Say why the LORD reduced the army (7:2)
Describe how the three hundred attacked (7:16-22)

nodes.t: Gideon pursues Midian and refuses to rule
nodes.d: Gideon calms Ephraim, punishes Succoth and Penuel for refusing him bread, kills the kings Zebah and Zalmunna, declines Israel's offer to rule, but makes an ephod that becomes a snare; after his death Israel turns again to Baal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Gideon did after the victory and what happened when he died?
ev: Say how Gideon answered the offer to rule (8:22-23)
Say what became a snare (8:27)
Say what Israel did after Gideon died (8:33-35)

nodes.t: Abimelech kills his brothers; Jotham's fable
nodes.d: Abimelech persuades Shechem to make him king and kills Gideon's seventy sons except Jotham, who tells a fable of the trees and the bramble and pronounces a curse.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Abimelech did and what Jotham said from Mount Gerizim?
ev: Say how Abimelech became king (9:1-6)
Retell Jotham's fable and the curse (9:7-21)

nodes.d: God sends an evil spirit between Abimelech and Shechem; Abimelech destroys Shechem and its tower, and at Thebez a woman drops a millstone on his head; the text says God repaid his wickedness and Jotham's curse came.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jotham's curse came true for Abimelech and Shechem?
ev: Say what happened between Abimelech and Shechem
Describe how Abimelech died (9:50-54)
Say how the text explains these events (9:56-57)

nodes.t: Tola, Jair, Ibzan, Elon and Abdon
nodes.d: Short notices list judges who ruled after Abimelech and Jephthah, with their tribes, years and burial places.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of the judges mentioned briefly in Judges?
ev: Name two or more of these judges and say how long they judged

nodes.t: Israel cries to the LORD under the Philistines and Ammon
nodes.d: Israel again serves other gods and is oppressed by the Philistines and Ammon; the LORD tells them to cry to their chosen gods, but when they confess and put away the foreign gods, his soul is grieved for their misery.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Israel responded when the LORD refused at first to deliver them?
ev: Say what the LORD answered first (10:11-14)
Say what Israel did next (10:15-16)

nodes.t: Jephthah is made head of Gilead
nodes.d: Jephthah, driven out by his half-brothers, is asked back by the elders of Gilead to fight Ammon; he first sends messengers recounting how Israel came to the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jephthah became leader of Gilead?
ev: Say why Jephthah was expelled and why he was recalled (11:1-8)
Summarise his message to the king of Ammon (11:12-27)

nodes.d: The Spirit of the LORD comes on Jephthah, who vows to offer whatever first comes from his house if the LORD gives victory; the LORD delivers Ammon, and his only daughter comes out to meet him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jephthah vowed and what followed?
ev: Say what Jephthah vowed (11:30-31)
Say who met him and how she answered (11:34-36)

nodes.d: The men of Ephraim complain that Jephthah did not call them; Gilead fights them and uses the word Shibboleth at the Jordan fords; Jephthah judges six years.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the word Shibboleth was used for?
ev: Say why Ephraim was angry (12:1)
Say how the Gileadites identified Ephraimites (12:5-6)

nodes.d: The angel of the LORD tells Manoah's barren wife that she will bear a son who will be a Nazarite and begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines; Manoah offers a burnt offering and Samson is born.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the angel of the LORD promised Manoah's wife?
ev: Say what the son was to avoid (13:4-5, 13:7)
Say what Manoah and his wife saw at the offering (13:19-21)

nodes.d: Samson wants a Philistine wife, kills a lion by the Spirit, and poses a riddle at his feast; his wife tells the answer, and he kills thirty men at Ashkelon and leaves; she is given to his companion.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of Samson's riddle?
ev: Retell the riddle and how it was answered
Note that 14:4 says this was of the LORD, seeking occasion against the Philistines

nodes.t: Samson burns the fields and fights at Lehi
nodes.d: Samson burns the Philistines' grain with foxes carrying firebrands after his wife is given away; Judah binds him and hands him over, but the Spirit comes on him and he kills a thousand with a jawbone; God provides water.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened between Samson, the Philistines and Judah?
ev: Say why Samson burned the Philistine fields
Say what Judah did and what Samson did at Lehi (15:9-17)
Say how Samson's thirst was met (15:18-19)

nodes.d: Samson carries off the gates of Gaza, then loves Delilah, who is bribed by the Philistine lords; after three false answers he reveals his Nazarite hair, it is cut, the LORD departs from him, and he is blinded and imprisoned.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Samson lost his strength?
ev: Say what Delilah asked and how Samson answered
Say what Samson told Delilah about his hair (16:17)
Say what happened when his hair was cut (16:19-21)

nodes.d: At the Philistines' feast to Dagon, the blind Samson prays to the LORD and pulls down the pillars, killing more in his death than in his life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Samson died?
ev: Say why the Philistines gathered (16:23-25)
Say what Samson prayed and did (16:28-30)

nodes.t: Micah's idols and his Levite priest
nodes.d: Micah of Ephraim returns stolen silver to his mother, makes images and an ephod, and hires a Levite from Bethlehem as his priest; the text notes there was no king and everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what was wrong in Micah's house?
ev: Say what Micah made and whom he hired as priest
Say what 17:6 says about Israel then

nodes.t: The Danites take Micah's priest and settle Laish
nodes.d: The tribe of Dan sends spies who meet Micah's Levite; six hundred armed Danites take Micah's images and priest, capture the peaceful city of Laish and rename it Dan.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the Danites came to live in the city of Dan?
ev: Say what the Danites took from Micah
Say what they did to Laish (18:27-29)

nodes.t: The Levite and his concubine at Gibeah
nodes.d: A Levite and his concubine lodge at Gibeah of Benjamin; men of the city assault the house, she is abused through the night and found dead at the door, and he sends her divided body through Israel; the text says no such deed had been seen since Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened at Gibeah and what the Levite did?
ev: Say where the events took place
Say how Israel reacted to the sign sent to all the tribes (19:29-30)

nodes.d: Israel assembles at Mizpeh and demands the guilty men of Gibeah; Benjamin refuses and defeats Israel twice, but after Israel inquires of the LORD and uses an ambush, Benjamin is nearly destroyed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the war between Israel and Benjamin went?
ev: Say why Israel went to war with Benjamin
Say what happened in the first two battles and the third (20:21-25, 20:35)
Say how many Benjamite men escaped (20:47)

nodes.d: Israel grieves that a tribe is missing; having sworn not to give their daughters to Benjamin, they take wives from Jabesh-gilead and from the daughters of Shiloh; the book ends noting there was no king in Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Israel dealt with the tribe of Benjamin after the war?
ev: Say what oath Israel had sworn (21:1)
Say how the remaining Benjamites got wives (21:10-23)
Say how the book ends (21:25)

nodes.d: Joshua records Israel crossing the Jordan after Moses' death (1:1-2), taking and dividing the land, and Joshua's closing call to serve the LORD at Shechem, ending with his death (24:29).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline the book of Joshua from the crossing of the Jordan to the covenant at Shechem?
ev: Say how the book begins with the death of Moses and ends with the death of Joshua
Name the three parts: entering and conquering, dividing the land, and the farewell charges

nodes.d: Caleb recalls Moses' oath at Kadesh and, at eighty-five, asks for the hill country of Hebron; Joshua blesses him, Caleb drives out the sons of Anak, and Othniel wins Debir and Achsah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Caleb received Hebron?
ev: Say why Caleb says he deserves Hebron (14:8-9)
Retell how Othniel won Achsah (15:16-17)

nodes.t: Choose this day: the covenant at Shechem
nodes.d: At Shechem Joshua recounts God's acts from Abraham to the conquest, urges Israel to choose whom to serve, makes a covenant with the people, and sets up a stone of witness before dying at 110.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at Shechem and what Joshua said about choosing whom to serve?
ev: Say what Joshua and his house decided (24:15)
Retell the history Joshua recounted (24:2-13)
Say what Joshua did that day and where he was buried (24:25-30)

nodes.d: Ruth, set in the days when the judges ruled, follows Naomi and her Moabite daughter-in-law Ruth from loss in Moab to marriage with Boaz in Bethlehem and the birth of Obed, the grandfather of David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise the book of Ruth from Moab to the birth of Obed?
ev: Say where the story is set and when
Say how the book ends with David's line (4:17-22)

nodes.d: 1 Samuel runs from the birth of Samuel to Saul's death on Mount Gilboa: Samuel as prophet and judge, Israel's request for a king, Saul's reign and rejection, and David's rise and flight from Saul.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 1 Samuel from Hannah's prayer to the death of Saul?
ev: Name the three main figures: Samuel, Saul and David
Say how the book begins and ends (1:1-20, 31:1-13)

nodes.t: The rest of the cloud: triumph and suffering by faith
nodes.d: The writer lists Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel and the prophets, and describes those who conquered and those who suffered, none of whom received the promise without us.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the writer says about those who by faith suffered and had not yet received the promise (11:35-40)?
ev: Name some people in 11:32
Contrast the two kinds of experience in 11:33-38

nodes.d: The letter to the Hebrews presents Jesus as God's Son, greater than angels and Moses, our great high priest after Melchizedek who mediates a better covenant by one sacrifice, and calls readers to faith and endurance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Hebrews teaches about Jesus and what the readers are told to do?
ev: Describe the main parts: the Son (1-2), Moses and rest (3-4), the high priest (4-7), the new covenant and sacrifice (8-10), faith (11), endurance and exhortations (12-13)
